newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank says to add liquidity at min 45 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank says to add liquidity at min 45 pct.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) said on Wednesday that it would add liquidity to the interbank money market through an overnight reverse repo tender at a minimum rate of 45 percent.

"This is not an easing of policy, but given the severe liquidity shortage on the market at the end of today's minimum reserve period, we were forced to add some liquidity," CNB bank board member Ludek Niedermeyer told Reuters.
Niedermeyer did not reveal how short the sector was, but he did say the operation would probably add a "little less" liqudity than was actually needed to full satisfy the market.
"This is not a signal that we are easing the pressure, but we have to support the smooth functioning of the money market," he said.
"We will act only in a way that will not give anyone additional space for buying foreign currency, but just to maintain the smooth functioning of payments," he added.
Last Friday the CNB raised its Lombard rate to 50 from 14 percent in an attempt to shore up the ailing crown.
On Tuesday, Prague interbank money market rates skyrocketed as banks looked to cover their positions before today's minimum reserve deadline. Overnight funds rose to over 100 percent.
"We are doing this only on an overnight basis to avoid any market distortion," Niedermeyer said.
The CNB also announced a one-week repo tender to drain funds with the maximum rate to determined by bids at the auction.
"We also announced the spot-week repo to help take liquidity out of the market," he said.
